'''Robert Luther Flurry Jr.''' (November 15, 1933 &ndash; September 3, 2008) was an American chemistry professor at the [[University of New Orleans]], noted for his advances in [[molecular orbital theory]] and [[quantum chemistry]].

== Early life and career ==
Flurry served in the [[U.S. Navy]] as a musician before pursuing his academic career. He received his [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]], [[Master of Science|M.S.]], and [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] degrees from [[Emory University]] and completed post-doctoral studies at the [[Illinois Institute of Technology]].<ref name="obit">{{cite news |title=Robert Luther Flurry Jr. (obituary) |work=The Times-Picayune |date=8 September 2008 |url=https://www.genealogybank.com/doc/obituaries/obit/12318B04ED1DCE00-12318B04ED1DCE00 |access-date=June 29, 2025 |via=GenealogyBank}}</ref>

In 1962, Flurry joined the faculty of the [[University of New Orleans]], where he remained until his retirement.<ref name="LSUNO">{{cite news

== Publications and impact ==
His 1969 study of electron donor–acceptor complexes is highly cited,<ref name="flurry1969">{{cite journal |last=Flurry |first=Robert L. |title=Molecular orbital theory of electron donor–acceptor complexes. II. Charged donors and acceptors |journal=Journal of Physical Chemistry |volume=73 |issue=7 |pages=2111–2117 |year=1969 |doi=10.1021/j100727a003}}</ref><ref name="acs27">“Molecular orbital theory of electron donor–acceptor complexes. II. Charged donors and acceptors,” *J. Phys. Chem.* 73(7):2111–2117 (1969); cited by 27 publications as of June 29, 2025, via ACS Publications.</ref> and his research on electron donor–acceptor complexes is noted in modern historical treatments of noncovalent interactions in chemistry.<ref name="sigmis">{{cite journal |last1=Politzer |first1=Peter |last2=Murray |first2=Jane S. |title=σ-Hole Interactions: Perspectives and Misconceptions |journal=Crystals |volume=7 |issue=7 |page=212 |year=2017 |doi=10.3390/cryst7070212|doi-access=free |bibcode=2017Cryst...7..212P }}</ref>

Flurry authored three chemistry textbooks that received significant attention in the academic community:
* {{cite book |last=Flurry |first=Robert L. |year=1968 |title=Molecular Orbital Theories of Bonding in Organic Molecules |publisher=Marcel Dekker |lccn=68-13563}}<ref name="reviews1">Reviews of ''Molecular Orbital Theories of Bonding in Organic Molecules'':
*P. Sykes, ''Nature'' 220(5331):833 (23 Nov 1968), {{doi|10.1038/220833b0}}
*Lemont B. Kier, ''Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences'', {{doi|10.1002/jps.2600580243}}
*W. Kutzelnigg, ''Angewandte Chemie'', {{bibcode|1969AngCh..81R.232K}}, {{doi|10.1002/anie.196902252}}
*W. J. Orville-Thomas, ''Journal of Molecular Structure'', {{bibcode|1970JMoSt...6..337O}}, {{doi|10.1016/0022-2860(70)90021-9}}
*F. L. Pilar, ''Journal of Chemical Education'', {{doi|10.1021/ed046pA204}}
*C. V. R., ''Current Science'', {{JSTOR|24073212}}
*H. E. Simmons, ''American Scientist'', {{JSTOR|27828547}}
</ref>

* {{cite book |last=Flurry |first=Robert L. |year=1980 |title=Symmetry Groups: Theory and Chemical Applications |publisher=Prentice-Hall |isbn=0-13-880013-8}}<ref name="reviews2"> Reviews of ''Symmetry Groups: Theory and Chemical Applications'':
*James L. Bills, ''Journal of Chemical Education'', {{doi|10.1021/ed058pA380.2}}
*Charles Dismukes, ''American Scientist'', {{JSTOR|27850363}}
</ref>

* {{cite book |last=Flurry |first=Robert L. |year=1983 |title=Quantum Chemistry: An Introduction |publisher=Prentice-Hall |isbn=0-13-747832-1}}<ref name="ru1985">Translated into Russian:
{{cite book |last=Фларри |first=Р. Л. |title=Квантовая химия. Введение |trans-title=Quantum Chemistry: An Introduction |translator-first1=Э. Д. |translator-last1=Герман |translator-first2=Е. == Death ==
Flurry died on September 3, 2008, from complications related to [[Parkinson's disease]] after a 25-year struggle with the condition.<ref name="obit" />
